Written by
Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®

For acreage buyers around Fort Langley and the rest of Langley, I check the ALR status, well, septic and flood information with you before you firm up. I've been a REALTOR® since 2015 and I'm in the top 1% of Fraser Valley REALTORS®. I've also closed more than $500M in sales.
In Paragon, the MLS® system used by local REALTORS®, Fort Langley is Langley sub-area F69. For houses in and around the village, see my
Fort Langley houses for sale
page.

Most buyers here pick a size band first. One to five acres usually means a house, a big yard and room for a shop, a garden or a few animals. Five to ten acres gives more room for horses, hobby farming or simply space between you and the neighbours, but there's more land to fence, drain and keep up. Tell me which band you want and I'll set up an alert for it.

Many rural properties around Fort Langley are in the Agricultural Land Reserve. Look up every address on the provincial ALR map before you plan around a second home, a suite or a business. ALR land comes with housing limits set by the ALC, and those rules can be stricter than Township zoning alone. I confirm what the ALC and the Township allow on that parcel before you rely on it.

Many acreages are on a private well and a septic system rather than municipal water and sewer. Ask for recent water test results and the well record, plan a flow test during your conditions, and find out when the septic tank was last pumped. Because Fort Langley sits on the Fraser, also check the Township's flooding information for the address before you remove subjects.

I grew up on a farm in Langley and live here again now, so I know what acreage upkeep really takes. Walk the whole property, not just the house, and look at fencing, drainage and outbuildings with the same care.

Derby Reach Regional Park has forest trails along the Fraser, and Brae Island Regional Park is a short trip from the village. Fort Langley Elementary is in the village; check catchments with the SD35 locator. My
Fort Langley guide
covers village life.

1. What size are the acreages on this page?
Houses on acreage in Fort Langley, from about 1 to 10 acres. Most buyers choose between the 1 to 5 acre and 5 to 10 acre bands.
2. Is Fort Langley acreage in the ALR?
Many rural properties around Fort Langley are. Check each address on the provincial ALR map.
3. Can I build a second home on an ALR acreage?
ALR land has housing limits set by the ALC, which can be stricter than Township zoning. Confirm with the ALC and the Township for that parcel.
4. Are Fort Langley acreages on city water?
Many are on a private well and septic. Ask for water tests and the well record, and plan a flow test and septic inspection.
5. Is Fort Langley in a floodplain?
Parts of the Township near the Fraser have flood considerations. Check the Township's flooding page for the address.
6. What parks are near Fort Langley?
Derby Reach and Brae Island regional parks, plus the Fort Langley National Historic Site.
7. How is this different from the Fort Langley houses page?
This page shows houses on acreage only. The houses page shows detached homes in and around the village.
